title: Cap. IX Arg. A vocatione Evangelica: absolute antecedent election/reprobation would make indiscriminate Gospel offers a simulation — therefore reprobation only after foresight of despised grace
pass_a_gloss: From the Evangelical vocation they so dispute. If God by an antecedent and absolute decree had elected some, reprobated some, he would act with simulation in offering grace indiscriminately unto men through evangelical ministers. For neither can it be commanded precisely unto the elect unto salvation that they believe under hope of obtaining salvation; because no one under a condition expects that which he knows to be absolutely ordained unto himself: nor can it be commanded unto the reprobate that they believe; for God would so exact of them that they believe a falsehood, namely that Christ suffered and died for them, and obtained life and reconciliation for them. Therefore it is to be established that no one is reprobated except from consideration and foresight of despised grace, and of final continuance in this obduration of heart and unbelief.
pass_b_english: From the Gospel call they argue thus. If God by an antecedent absolute decree had elected some and reprobated others, he would be acting with simulation when he offers grace indiscriminately through evangelical ministers. For the elect unto salvation cannot be commanded to believe under hope of obtaining salvation — no one awaits under a condition what he knows is absolutely ordained for him. Nor can the reprobate be commanded to believe — God would then require them to believe a falsehood: that Christ suffered and died for them and obtained life and reconciliation for them. Therefore, they say, no one is reprobated except from regard and foresight of despised grace and final persistence in that hardness of heart and unbelief.
source_text: A vocatione Evangelica sic disputant. Si Deus decreto antecedaneo et absoluto quosdam elegisset, quosdam reprobasset, ageret simulate gratiam offerendo hominibus indiscriminatim per ministros evangelicos. Nam neque precise ad salutem electis mandari potest ut credant sub spe salutis adipiscendae; quia nemo sub conditione exspectat, quod sibi scit absolute ordinatum: neque reprobatis mandari potest ut credant; nam Deus sic exigeret ab eis ut falsum crederent, scilicet Christum pro illis fuisse passum et mortuum, illisque vitam et reconciliationem impetrasse. Ergo statuendum est, neminem reprobari nisi ex consideratione et praevisione spretae gratiae, et finalis permansionis in hac cordis obduratione et infidelitate.
